back_translation: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: behold, a basket of ripe summer fruit.
He said, 'Amos, what do you see?' I answered, 'A basket of ripe summer fruit.' Then the LORD said to me, 'The end has come upon My people Israel; I will never again pass them by.'
The Lord GOD declares: In that day the songs of the temple will turn to wailing. There will be many corpses, flung out in every place. Silence!
Hear this, you who trample the needy and destroy the poor of the land,

saying, 'When will the new moon be over, that we may sell grain? And when will the Sabbath end, that we may open the wheat for sale—making the ephah small and the shekel large, and cheating with dishonest scales,
so that we may buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell even the chaff mixed with the wheat?'
The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: 'I will never forget any of their deeds.'
Shall not the land tremble for this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, then be tossed about and sink again like the Nile of Egypt.
The Lord GOD declares: In that day I will make the sun set at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; I will make everyone wear sackcloth around the waist and shave every head bald; I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
The Lord GOD declares: Behold, the days are coming when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.
People will wander from sea to sea, and from north to east; they will roam about seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria, and say, 'As your god lives, O Dan,' and 'As the way of Beersheba lives'—they will fall and never rise again.
